key_insight: Embedding neural networks directly into PDEs allows recovery of unknown functional components from observational data: as the networks are trained they can approximate those functions to arbitrary accuracy.
problem_solved: PDE models often include unknown functions (not just scalar parameters) that are difficult or impossible to measure, which limits predictive use of the models. This work provides a workflow to learn those unknown functions from data, enabling accurate model recovery and prediction.
method: Represent unknown functional coefficients inside the PDE as neural networks (surrogate functions) integrated into the model.
Train the embedded networks end-to-end using observational data by minimizing discrepancy between PDE-predicted and observed system behavior.
Demonstrate (theoretically/empirically) that the trained networks can approximate the true unknown functions arbitrarily well given sufficient data and model capacity.
impact: Makes inverse problems for PDEs tractable when unknowns are functions rather than scalars, enabling richer data-driven discovery and more accurate modeling across physics, biology, and engineering. Provides a flexible, scalable approach for practitioners to learn spatially/temporally varying model components from data.
visual_elements: Block diagram showing a PDE with an embedded neural network module, arrows from data into training loop, and output labeled 'learned function'.
Side-by-side plot of true vs learned functional coefficient (curve) with an accompanying error-convergence chart.
Field/solution comparison heatmaps: PDE solution using true function vs solution using learned function to visualize predictive fidelity.
Workflow flowchart: data collection → embed NN in PDE → training/optimization → validation and deployment.
paper_title: Learning functional components of PDEs from data using neural networks
paper_authors: Torkel E. Loman, Yurij Salmaniw, Antonio Leon Villares, Jose A. Carrillo, Ruth E. Baker
